name: lapis-bases
description: Create and edit Lapis Bases (.base) documents, note-property filters, formulas and views.

# Lapis Bases

Read [documents and Lapis views](references/DOCUMENTS_AND_VIEWS.md) for the saved
model, native board/activity options and import differences. Read
[functions and expressions](references/FUNCTIONS_REFERENCE.md) for the tested
Lapis query dialect, collection callbacks and date semantics.

A `.base` file describes views over existing vault files; it does not contain
copies of the underlying notes. Read the document and representative note
frontmatter before changing filters or formulas. Preserve unknown document and
view fields and unrelated note properties.

Document-wide filters use the plural `filters` field. Per-view filters use
singular `filter` in the native saved model; import also accepts plural
`filters` inside a view. Use the native model for new documents:

```yaml
filters:
  and:
    - 'file.ext == "md"'
formulas:
  total: "price * quantity"
properties:
  note.status:
    displayName: Status
views:
  - type: table
    name: Projects
    filter:
      and:
        - 'status == "active"'
    order:
      - file.name
      - status
      - formula.total
    sort:
      - property: file.name
        direction: ASC
```

Use `and`, `or` or `not` arrays for filter groups. Invalid groups fail rather
than becoming an unrestricted query. Quote expressions so YAML punctuation
remains expression data. Note properties may be bare in expressions; use
`note.` for note-property display metadata and `formula.` for formula columns.

Lapis includes table, cards, list, kanban, activity and map registrations.
Use the reference for actual view options and preserve unknown/custom view
types. Formula support follows the installed Lapis runtime, not every upstream
function or JavaScript expression.

Parse the YAML after editing, confirm referenced formulas exist, and inspect
representative included and excluded files. Open the resulting Base in Lapis
to check that its actual rows, ordering and view match the request.

Adapted for Lapis from [Obsidian skills](https://github.com/obsidianmd/obsidian-skills).
See [upstream license](LICENSE.txt).

# Lapis Base documents and views

Read this when creating a Base or changing its presentation. A Base queries
vault files; rows are not separate records stored in the .base file.

## Saved document contract

| Field      | Meaning                                                |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| filters    | Document-wide predicate, applied to every view         |
| formulas   | Named computed expressions, referenced as formula.name |
| properties | Display metadata; note properties use note.name here   |
| summaries  | Named summary definitions                              |
| activeView | Name of the selected view, not its type or array index |
| views      | Ordered view definitions with unique useful names      |

Use singular filter inside a new view. Lapis imports the plural filters alias
but writes the native singular key; do not leave two competing view predicates.
A malformed Boolean group is an error, not an unrestricted query.

```yaml
filters:
  and:
    - 'file.ext == "md"'
formulas:
  total: "price * quantity"
properties:
  note.status:
    displayName: Status
activeView: Board
views:
  - type: table
    name: Table
    filter:
      and:
        - 'status == "active"'
    order: [file.name, status, formula.total]
    sort:
      - property: file.name
        direction: ASC
  - type: kanban
    name: Board
    order: [file.name, status, formula.total]
    groupBy:
      property: status
      direction: ASC
    titleProperty: file.name
    descriptionProperty: description
    tagsProperty: file.tags
    filter:
      and: []
```

## Built-in Lapis views

Table, cards, list, kanban, activity and map are registered view types. A
registered type does not imply that every upstream option is implemented.

- Table uses order, sort, columnSize and rowHeight. Its layout can be table or
  cards; preserve that setting when editing an existing file.
- Cards supports image, imageFit (contain or cover), imageAspectRatio and cardSize.
- List uses the selected properties, defaulting to file.name when order is empty.
- Kanban groups notes and renders Markdown-backed cards. titleProperty,
  descriptionProperty, tagsProperty, chipProperty and badgeProperty map note
  data into the card; they are not arbitrary rendered HTML.
- Activity uses the same card mappings and an explicit dateProperty, or the
  first selected date/datetime property. Preserve the intended date selection.
- Map configuration is retained, but the current renderer shows an explicit
  unavailable state. Do not promise map tiles, coordinates or geographic editing.

Lapis board lane settings include columnOrder, columnMeta and columnFilters.
Their keys are persisted lane identities: preserve existing IDs rather than
inventing them from display labels. columnFilters contains native filter groups.
Unknown view types retain their authored type and show an unsupported-view state;
do not silently replace them with a table.

When patching YAML, merge the requested fields and preserve unrelated content.
Do not use a normalizer as a lossless serializer for arbitrary extension fields.
Validate examples through the installed Lapis parser and inspect actual rows.

# Lapis Bases expressions and functions

Read this for filters, computed properties and dates. This is the Lapis query
boundary, not a JavaScript evaluator or a promise of complete upstream parity.

## Names and predicates

Note properties can be bare (price) or prefixed (note.price). File metadata uses
file.name, file.path, file.ext, file.ctime and file.mtime. A formula reference
uses formula.total; formula["display name"] handles a non-identifier name.
For a note key containing punctuation, use note["review score"].

Comparison operators include ==, !=, >, >=, < and <=. Use and/or/not YAML groups
for combined predicates. Lapis lowers == at the query boundary while retaining
quoted expression text. JavaScript strict equality === is rejected. Missing or
circular formula references are errors; do not replace them with a broad filter.

```yaml
filters:
  and:
    - 'file.ext == "md"'
    - 'note["review score"] >= 3'
    - not:
        - 'status == "archived"'
formulas:
  total: "price * quantity"
  label: 'if(formula.total > 100, "large", "small")'
views:
  - type: table
    name: Reviewed
    filter:
      and: []
    order: [file.name, formula.total, formula.label]
```

## Runtime-supported helper families

| Task            | Functions and examples                                                                    |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Text            | lower, title, trim, split, replace, repeat, startsWith, endsWith, matches                 |
| Contains        | contains, containsAny, containsAll; containsAnyOf/containsAllOf remain aliases            |
| Numbers         | number, abs, ceil, floor, round, toFixed, min, max                                        |
| Conditions      | if(condition, yes, no), isEmpty, isTruthy, isType, toString                               |
| File predicates | file.hasTag, file.hasLink, file.hasProperty, file.inFolder                                |
| Display values  | file, link, image, html, icon, asFile, asLink                                             |
| Collections     | list, length, map, filter, reduce, flat, join, reverse, slice, sort, unique, keys, values |
| Time            | date, duration, today, now, relative, format, time                                        |

Formatting helpers produce display values. They do not create files, fetch an
image, authorize HTML execution or persist changes to a note.

## Collection semantics

Lists support method notation and callback-local value, index and acc. Callback
expressions are data; do not write JavaScript lambdas. Examples exercised by the
Lapis query engine:

| Expression                     | Result   |
| ------------------------------ | -------- |
| [1,2,3].contains(2)            | true     |
| [1,2,3,4].filter(value > 2)    | [3,4]    |
| [1,2,3].map(value + index)     | [1,3,5]  |
| [1,2,3].reduce(acc + value, 0) | 6        |
| [30,1,2].sort()                | [1,2,30] |
| [1,2,2,3].unique()             | [1,2,3]  |
| [1,[2,3]].flat()               | [1,2,3]  |

A list literal creates a new outer list and preserves null elements. list(anArray)
retains the existing list semantics. Reverse and sort do not mutate note data.
Within a nested callback, value/index/acc belong to that callback; use note.key
for an outer note property. An empty list and numeric zero have different
emptiness/truthiness behavior; do not use truthiness to detect a missing number.

## Date details that matter in Lapis

Date helpers use the Lapis date runtime. today() is midnight in the configured
zone; now() includes the current time. date("2025-01-02").format("YYYY-MM-DD")
produces the calendar date. dateValue.time() produces HH:mm:ss, while
now().date() selects the calendar day. Formatting tokens follow the supported
Moment-style compatibility layer, not JavaScript Date formatting.

number(date("1970-01-02T00:00:00Z")) is 86400000 (milliseconds). Duration units
are case-sensitive: duration("1M") is one month and duration("1m") one minute.
Do not assume daylight-saving or month arithmetic is a fixed millisecond count.
Use explicit dates/zones in reproducible examples and check boundary cases.
